transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I'm here because I've been having a really hard time listening when people talk to me. Even when someone is speaking directly to my face, it feels like my mind just drifts off and I miss what they said. It's starting to cause a lot of issues in my daily life, so I wanted to get some help.

Have you had trouble paying attention and listening like this since childhood, or did it start later in life? If it started later, was it around a time when you were feeling very worried or down most days?

Honestly, this has been happening for as long as I can remember, definitely since I was a kid under the age of 12. It didn't start later in life, and I don't think it has anything to do with feeling worried or down. It's just always been a struggle for me.
Do these attention problems happen in more than one setting, like both at work or school and at home or in social situations? Can you give one example?
I'm not quite sure, to be honest. I haven't really thought about whether it happens more in specific different settings or if there is a pattern to it.
Besides drifting off when people talk, do you often have trouble staying organized, finishing tasks, or keeping track of things like appointments, keys, or paperwork?

I definitely have a lot of trouble keeping track of my things and constantly lose my keys, wallet, or important paperwork. I'm not really sure about general organization or finishing tasks, but I am always misplacing items I need for my daily activities.
Can you think of one recent example of this causing a problem at work or school, and one example at home or in your personal life?

At work last week, I lost some important paperwork that I needed for a meeting, which ended up delaying the whole project. At home, I misplaced my keys just yesterday and ended up locking myself out of my apartment for two hours.
Do you also often make careless mistakes, avoid tasks that take a lot of mental effort, or get easily distracted by things going on around you?

I do get easily distracted by things going on around me, or even just by my own unrelated thoughts drifting in. However, I don't really find myself making careless mistakes or avoiding tasks that take a lot of mental effort.
Do you often start tasks but have trouble finishing them because your attention drifts, even when you want to get them done?

Yes, my attention drifts a lot when I'm trying to focus on tasks because I get so easily distracted by noises around me or my own unrelated thoughts. Because of that, it can be really hard to actually get things finished.
Do you often forget appointments or daily responsibilities, or find that even when someone speaks directly to you, it feels like you didn’t fully hear what they said?

Yes, I definitely struggle with that second part; it often feels like I didn't fully hear or process what someone said, even when they're speaking directly to me. However, forgetting appointments or daily responsibilities isn't really a major issue for me.
Do you also tend to feel restless, fidget a lot, interrupt people, or act before thinking, or is this mainly an attention problem?

It is definitely mainly an attention problem. I don't experience restlessness, fidgeting, or interrupting people at all. My struggles are really focused on things like being easily distracted, constantly losing my things, and having a hard time listening.

They deny hyperactive/impulsive symptoms, which makes the predominantly inattentive presentation more likely and argues against the combined or predominantly hyperactive/impulsive presentations. No evidence emerged suggesting mood, psychotic, trauma-related, obsessive-compulsive, eating, or primary anxiety disorders as a better explanation.
